items.title: Doctor Who returns
items.line: Doctor Who came back on BBC One on 26 March 2005 with "Rose", Christopher Eccleston and Billie Piper, written by Russell T Davies. The final tally was 10.81 million viewers.

items.title: YouTube
items.line: YouTube was founded on 14 February 2005 by three ex-PayPal staff. The first upload, "Me at the zoo", went up on 23 April: Jawed Karim at the San Diego Zoo.

items.title: Live 8 in Hyde Park
items.line: On 2 July 2005 Pink Floyd's classic line-up played together for the first time in 24 years. Bob Geldof hosted, and the show overran its 21:30 close to nearly half past midnight.

items.title: The 2005 Ashes
items.line: England won the Ashes 2-1, their first win since 1986-87. The Edgbaston Test was decided by 2 runs, the narrowest margin in Ashes history, and Flintoff took 24 wickets.

items.title: iPod nano
items.line: Apple announced the iPod nano on 7 September 2005 to replace the mini. It was 6.9 mm thin and held 2 or 4 GB, with a 1 GB version added in February 2006.

items.title: Xbox 360
items.line: The Xbox 360 went on sale in the US and Canada on 22 November 2005 at $399 for the Premium pack and $299 for Core. Europe got it on 2 December, at 279 pounds.
